messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming.decode tail latency p99 spike detected for prod cluster us-west-2 - p99 1800ms (baseline 320ms) — increased error/stall rate 0.9% -> 4.7% — alert id: INC-5419876543
Anya Patel: seeing it, joining. pinging runtime and s-repro folks.
Anya Patel: initial check — most of the spikes are in decoder service (gpu-pool-2), streaming endpoints. p95 jumped 120ms -> 420ms in last 20m. p99 heavy tail around 1.5-2s.
Mike Chen: copying perf traces now. grabbing `trace_id` from router for a few failing requests.
Nina Sato: I see a sudden jump in kernel-load failures and long compile paths in the logs around 09:12 UTC. stack: linker nvrtc compile -> fallback to slower kernel path.
Ben Ortiz: any recent rollouts? I see a TRT runtime bump 8.2.1 landed ~08:50 UTC to canary group, and a flash-attn 2.0 build with new CUDA kernels at 08:47.
Samir Das: also a variant of the decode compile flags was flipped in the last build: `-O3 -ffp-contract=fast -DTRT_FAST_MATMUL` replaced previous `-Ofast` variant. build id r1523.
Anya Patel: good find. correlate: TRT8 bump -> flash-attn kernels -> compile flag tweak. timeline fits.
runtime-l2: rolling up kernel build logs now. early signs: nvrtc JIT emitting slightly larger kernels that thrashed L2 on longer sequences — leads to paging in device memory and stalls.
Mike Chen: reproduced locally on a small repro with long streaming prefix. when flash-attn kernels load, we see bursts of page-fault-like stalls in nvlink traffic and JIT compile time spikes (~200-400ms).
Anya Patel: customer impact? which tenants saw errors?
Nina Sato: ingress metrics: 18 accounts had >0.1% stall rate; 3 enterprise accounts saw >1% and reported degraded streaming continuity. our reg monitor flagged them. no 5xx surge, mostly long-tail stalls and chunked responses.
Ben Ortiz: mitigation idea: route traffic off the updated kernel variant to a pinned older runtime (trt 8.1 + flash-attn 1.x) until we hotfix compile flags. can we spin a traffic routing rule?
Anya Patel: yes — runtime supports per-customer routing. I'll create a quick policy to prefer `runtime:trt8-8.1-flash1` for streaming endpoints for 1h.
Anya Patel: (creating policy)
Anya Patel: ```
# temporary routing override
route:
  predicate: route.request.streaming == true
  prefer: runtime.trt8-8.1-flash1
  ttl: 3600
```
Anya Patel: applied. :white_check_mark: routing change propagated to edge gateways.
deploy-bot: deploy policy applied to edge gateways in us-west-2 (18 hosts) — rollout completed in 38s.
Samir Das: while routing change helps, we still need root cause — likely JIT kernel size + new compile flag causing register pressure/paging on certain sequence lengths.
Mike Chen: I pushed a hotpatch to the decoder workers: set env `FLASH_ATTENTION_DISABLE_JIT=1` for the affected pool and restarted pods gradually to avoid cold start stampede.
deploy-bot: restarted 12 decoder pods in gpu-pool-2, restart latency ~80s each, gradual.
Nina Sato: logs after restart show immediate reduction in nvrtc compile spikes. p95 dropped to ~200ms within 5m. p99 down to ~480ms.
Anya Patel: good. customer-reported continuity improved. asking SRE to monitor for the next 30m then we'll decide rollback vs config tweak.
Ben Ortiz: next steps for engineering: reproduce with exact r1523 build and full long-prefix streaming workload. hypothesis: `-DTRT_FAST_MATMUL` interacts with flash-attn fused kernel generation causing oversized kernels on sm90 GPUs leading to L2 thrash.
Samir Das: propose two parallel actions: (1) revert the compile flag in the build (quick), (2) patch nvrtc compilation options to limit kernel unrolling (`--maxrregcount=64`) and test perf.
Anya Patel: agree. Ben/Nina handle reproduction + PR to revert flag. Samir/Mike handle JIT constraints and patch. I'll coordinate customer comms and holdbridge with support.
Mike Chen: assigning self to incident until 0815 UTC for mitigation follow-up. will loop in runtime-l2 for deeper memory-scheduler tracing.
Nina Sato: started local reproduce harness: command used: `python tests/repro_stream.py --model vicuna-13b --seq 2048 --batch 4 --flash-attn r1523` — initial run shows regressed tail at ~p99 1.2s, switching to pre-r1523 reduces to 360ms.
runtime-l2: gathering low-level traces (ptp, pcie counters, nvlink) and will upload flame graphs. ETA 25m.
Anya Patel: support update drafted: short note explaining we detected a runtime kernel/compile change causing transient streaming stalls — routing and hotpatch applied, monitoring continued. will mark as 'mitigated' once p99 stable for 30m.
Samir Das: created draft PR to revert `-DTRT_FAST_MATMUL` -> PR #4221. CI builds queued. If CI green we can roll forward the revert within 2h.
Ben Ortiz: recording for postmortem: timeline, builds (r1521 -> r1523), kernel artifacts, nvrtc logs, reproduction steps, customers impacted list (18 accounts, 3 enterprise).
Anya Patel: handoff — I'm going offline at 07:50 UTC. Mike is primary until 0815. runtime-l2 please keep tracing and alert if p99 > 800ms or stall rate > 1.5%.
Mike Chen: got it. I'll follow up with a short runbook and action items for postmortem.
Anya Patel: final quick notes: probable root cause: combination of TRT upgrade + new flash-attn kernels + aggressive compile flags producing oversized JIT kernels that trigger device-level stalls/paging on long prefixes. Mitigations applied: routing override, env hotpatch (disable JIT flash-attn), restart of decoder pool. Next steps: revert flag PR, nvrtc compile constraining patch, extended soak tests, postmortem & customer follow-up.
Mike Chen: I'll open the incident ticket (INC-5419876543) with summary and assign owners. handing off now. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident INC-5419876543 created and assigned to Mike Chen. priority: P2.
Anya Patel: thanks all — great quick coordination. :pray:
